attempts.explanation: When arbitrating and a valid new requester is found (found=1), the RTL leaves the grant signal unassigned or unchanged rather than updating it to the one-hot encoding of the new winner (`1 << pick`), which violates behavior rule 2.
When arbitrating and a winner is found (`found` is high), the RTL does not update `grant` with the newly picked requester (`1 << pick`), leaving `grant` at 0. This violates behavior rule 2.

When arbitrating and finding a new winner (`found`), the RTL leaves the `grant` register unassigned (executing an empty statement `;`), causing `grant` to become 0 instead of updating to `1 << pick`. This violates the arbitration behavior specification.
